Paramythia Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Konstantinou Karamanli, Greece

Demolished. Archaeological evidence points to Jewish presence in Paramythia across three distinct periods — Byzantine times, the 12th century, and again from the early 19th century — with the community engaged in the textile trade and playing an outsized role in the local economy relative to its tiny size, numbering just 15 people (of nearly 15,700 total) by 1928. All but 2 of them perished in the Holocaust, swept up together with the much larger Jewish community of Ioannina in the March 1944 deportation.
